scenario.title: Hot Reset from the host
scenario.description: At 35 ms, with every link at Gen4, software sets the Secondary Bus Reset bit on the root port. The root port signals Hot Reset with TS1s, the switch upstream port follows, and the switch propagates the reset to its downstream ports. Every link goes down, retrains from Detect at 2.5 GT/s, equalizes again and ends exactly as in S01.
scenario.symptom: Every device behind the root port disappeared for a while and then came back by itself.
commands: at 35 ms on RP, software: Hot Reset requested (Secondary Bus Reset)

expected.summary: All switch links retrain after the Hot Reset; the final state matches S01 (A and B at Gen4 x16, C at Gen4 x4, 7 functions).

scenario.what_to_look_for: At 35 ms RP logs "software: Hot Reset requested", enters Recovery to signal it, and moves to the red Hot Reset state; USP follows when it receives TS1s with the Hot Reset bit. The switch then directs DSP1 and DSP2 into Hot Reset too. After the 2 ms Hot Reset timer each link goes to Detect, DL_Link_Active drops, equalization status bits are cleared, and the whole bring-up from S01 repeats (including equalization at both rates). link_down_count is 1 on links A, B and C.
scenario.what_this_means: Hot Reset is an in-band reset carried by training sets. It resets everything below the port that issues it, so all links below retrain from scratch. A link that goes down because of a deliberate reset looks very similar to an unexpected link-down in the timeline; the difference is the software command (and Hot Reset state) right before it.
likely_root_causes: Software or firmware issued a Secondary Bus Reset (driver recovery, device reset, VM assignment).
Error recovery (for example AER or DPC handling) reset the hierarchy.
A setpci/Bridge Control write during debugging.
how_to_debug: Check the kernel log for reset messages around the time devices disappeared (driver resets, AER recovery, 'secondary bus reset').
Read Bridge Control on the root port (setpci -s <bdf> BRIDGE_CONTROL) to see the Secondary Bus Reset bit while debugging.
After the reset, confirm that LnkSta returns to the same speed/width as before (compare with the S01 baseline).
If devices do not come back after a reset, debug them like a cold bring-up (Detect/Polling first).
mystery_hints: Was there a software action right before the links went down?
Which red state appears on the root port?
scenario.mystery_cause: Software issued a Hot Reset (Secondary Bus Reset) on the root port; everything below retrained.
